method: Three fresh implicit, unfunded NEAR wallets per sequential baseline, combined completion/session-observation, and restored control arm. Custody, Runtime and placement stay fixed. Candidate SDK and matching iframe are injected into the browser at the staging origins. API requests use deployed staging Workers. Baseline uses the accepted Phase 6AM SDK. The candidate harness uses the React registration wrapper; the baseline invokes the same registration through the raw SDK.

independentSignatureVerification.verifier: Node.js crypto Ed25519 with independent NEP-413 Borsh encoding

limitations: Three samples per arm do not establish tail percentiles or a latency guarantee.
Sequential arms include provider scheduling and network variation.
Fresh wallets do not prove cold Workers. Cold starts were not controlled.
Application and iframe assets are served by the browser harness. Asset download latency is excluded.
Browser elapsed time includes automation. Invocation wall time can include background work.
Nested spans overlap. Yao protocol spans include transport.
The new session-issue timer includes home completion. Compare whole finalization spans across versions.
Bound-root D1 counters cover a subset of database work. Full registration D1 counts remain unmeasured.
Requested APAC placement does not prove physical colocation.
R155C transport is excluded from every arm.
setupReadbackNote: The first setup attempt saw a stale Console deployment readback and restored its only changed assignment before any benchmark ran. Deployment history contained only this experiment's setup and restore operations. Bounded read-only retries resolved subsequent readback convergence.
retentionDecision:
Keep both changes. The request reductions are demonstrated in every sample.
Candidate finalization has the lowest arm median: **2.234s**, compared with
**2.345s** before and **2.504s** after. The observed differences are **111ms**
and **270ms**. Three sequential samples per arm do not isolate a repeatable
causal saving from network and scheduling variation.

Registration to verified signature measures **14.467s → 11.532s → 12.160s**.
The restored control also improves over the initial baseline. Therefore, the
entire baseline-to-candidate difference cannot be assigned to these changes.
SDK registration measures **10.355s → 8.773s → 8.887s**. These results support
retaining fewer calls, with modest observed finalization gains. The **3–4s**
registration-to-signature target remains unmet. This comparison completes the
three independent Gateway, Console, and SDK items in Phases 6AP–6AQ. R155C's
separate A/B transport measurement remains the next major comparison.
